sections.changelog:
Changed

  • **The search demands every word and loosens only when that leaves nothing to look at.** The floor was decided before the query ran: "balanced" meant a third of the words could be dropped, always, whether or not the strict reading had plenty of answers — and the word dropped was whichever the ranking cared least about, routinely the one naming the part. On a 13k-product parts catalogue that turned "iPhone 16 pro lcd" into 130 results: flex cables, protective glasses, back covers and SIM trays all clear "iPhone 16 pro" and only 18 were a display at all, against 9 displays for that exact model in the catalogue. The pass now starts at full coverage and steps down one rung at a time, stopping as soon as a rung returns more than a couple of rows; the strictness setting has become the bottom of that descent rather than its start, so nothing gets looser than before. This is the order the established engines use — Typesense relaxes at its `drop_tokens_threshold` (default 1), Algolia removes words only when a query returns nothing. The threshold matters: measured over 15 cases with a written-down ground truth, relaxing below 3 results scored F1 0.81 against 0.70 when relaxing below 8, because on a parts catalogue a two-result answer to "lcd g980 s20" is the right answer, not a shortage.

Added

  • **Results keep to the product type the query names (*Relevance → Keep only the named product type*, on by default).** Demanding every word is not enough when a catalogue writes what a product is and then what it fits: "Шлейф для iPhone 16 Pro" contains every word of "iPhone 16 pro lcd" once "дисплей" and "lcd" are synonyms, and "Рамка дисплея" says display while being a frame. The head noun of the title answers both — the frame's head is "рамка", the cable's is "шлейф", neither is a word the shopper typed. Leading adjectives are skipped by their ending, so "Защитное стекло" and "Стекло защитное" both resolve to "стекло". Applied only when some result does lead with a queried word, so a query naming no part type is untouched, and it stands down entirely when nothing matches, so a catalogue writing "iPhone 14 дисплей" instead keeps working. Measured across the two changes on the live catalogue: "iPhone 16 pro lcd" 130 results at 7% precision → **9 results at 100%**, "iPhone 13 pro экран" 223 → 16 at 100%, "iPhone 14 батарея" 427 → 30 at 100%, with recall staying at 100% throughout — no correct product is lost, only the noise around it. Average F1 over nine ground-truth cases: 0.37 → **0.95**.
  • **The results filter panel is picked apart in the settings (*Behaviour → Results page*).** The panel always showed all three filters, whether or not they meant anything on the catalogue: a shop filing everything under one category, or one whose brands are not a taxonomy, got a group of dead weight above the values that matter. Each of the three — categories, brands, price — now has its own switch, and its own field for the heading, so the panel can say "Найдено в разделах" where the shop's own word for a category is a section. An empty field keeps the built-in heading, and an installation that never touched the setting shows all three exactly as before. A turned-off group costs nothing: neither its terms nor the price range are queried. Turning off the group that holds the category chosen before the search does not quietly widen the results — the narrowing travels as a hidden field, and "Reset" still lifts it.
  • **A relevance benchmark (`tests/relevance-bench.php`).** Scenario tests answer "is it broken"; this answers "is it good".

Fixed

  • **The dropdown's own settings no longer decide what the results page filters by.** Both screens ask the same matcher for the categories and brands a query hits, and that matcher checked *Coverage → Matching categories / Matching brands* — the two switches that govern the live dropdown's groups. A shop that had turned those off to keep the dropdown lean also lost the filter panel's category and brand groups, with nothing on the results-page settings to explain why. The check moved to the dropdown, which is whose setting it is; the panel reads its own. Their section is now called *Groups in the dropdown* rather than *Categories in results*, which read like it governed the results page. Each case pairs a query with a ground truth — a SQL condition selecting what a human would accept — and the run reports precision, recall and F1 per strategy, so a ranking change is judged by numbers instead of by reading the first screen. Runs read-only against any catalogue: `MVWEB_SS_BENCH=cases.json wp eval-file tests/relevance-bench.php`.
